name: Prize crossword No 26,974
preamble: Each clue leads to two solutions, one or both of which contain a trio (or in two cases a quartet) of successive letters of the alphabet, appearing either forwards or backwards. In one case, these letters involve the beginning and end of the alphabet; in another, the letters to be included are a mix of three successive letters. These groups of three or four letters are to be included in the full version of the solution to be entered in the grid, but are omitted from the wordplay in the clues.

clue.text: My admission to being out of date causes stalemate around a neat ancient Iranian city

indicators.note: turned around and about, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.clueFragment: My admission to being out of date
blocks.note: someone owning up to being old hat would say 'I'm passé'
ANEAT taken as written to be rearranged, plus CBA, the preamble's backward run, which no clue word supplies

explanation.surface: Someone confessing they are behind the times breaks a deadlock somewhere in old Persia.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give ETANA, and the preamble's backward run CBA slips in after the E. Ecbatana was the capital of ancient Media, now Hamadan in Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate is a deadlock where neither side can make progress; Ecbatana is a historic Persian city.
